Q24190721.label: 2019 Canadian federal election
Q24190721.summary: The 2019 Canadian federal election was held on October 21, 2019. Members of the House of Commons were elected to the 43rd Canadian Parliament. In keeping with the maximum four-year term under a 2007 amendment to the Canada Elections Act, the writs of election for the 2019 election were issued by Governor General Julie Payette on September 11, 2019.

Q769.label: Grenada
Q769.desc: island sovereign state in the Caribbean Sea
Q769.summary: Grenada is an archipelagic country of the West Indies in the eastern Caribbean Sea. The southernmost of the Windward Islands, Grenada is directly south of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines and about 100 miles (160 km) north of Trinidad and the South American mainland.

Q7401729.label: 1997 Saint Lucian general election
Q7401729.desc: General election results for Saint Lucia in 1997
Q7401729.summary: General elections were held in Saint Lucia on 23 May 1997. The result was a victory for the Saint Lucia Labour Party, which won sixteen of the seventeen seats. Voter turnout was 66.1%.

Q7932161.label: 1972 Vincentian general election
Q7932161.desc: election in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
Q7932161.summary: General elections were held in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines on 7 April 1972. The result was a tie between the People's Political Party and the Saint Vincent Labour Party, which both won six seats. Despite being a former member of the SVLP, the sole independent MP James Fitz-Allen Mitchell formed a government with the PPP. Voter turnout was 75.6%.

Q6071553.label: 1943 Irish general election
Q6071553.summary: The 1943 Irish general election to the 11th Dáil was held on Wednesday, 23 June, having been called on 31 May by proclamation of President Douglas Hyde on the advice of Taoiseach Éamon de Valera. It took place in 34 parliamentary constituencies for 138 seats in Dáil Éireann, the house of representatives of the Oireachtas. Fianna Fáil lost its overall majority of seats. The outgoing 10th Dáil was dissolved on 26 June, although it had not met after 26 May.

Q16821505.label: Andorran political reform referendum, 1977
Q16821505.summary: A referendum on political reforms was held in Andorra on 28 October 1977. Voters were presented with six options, but none received a majority and over 30% of votes cast were left blank. A second referendum on political reform was held the following year.

Q7232769.label: 1969 Portuguese legislative election
Q7232769.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Portugal on 26 October 1969. The elections were announced on 12 August, and were the first under the Prime Minister Marcello Caetano, appointed in the previous year to replace the long-term Prime Minister António de Oliveira Salazar, who had been left incapacitated after a stroke. The ruling National Union won all seats with an official turnout of 62.5%.

Q125894913.label: Assassination of Abdel Aziz al-Rantisi
Q125894913.summary: On the evening of 17 April 2004, the leader of Hamas in the Gaza Strip, Abdel Aziz al-Rantisi, aged 56, was assassinated by missiles fired by Israeli warplanes on the car he was traveling in. In addition two of his bodyguards were killed. The operation was considered part of a campaign to eliminate the leaders of the groups fighting in the uprising.

Q43777.label: 2010 Haiti earthquake
Q43777.img: Ruins of Haiti National Palace - Port au Prince 2012.jpg
Q43777.summary: A catastrophic magnitude 7.0 Mw earthquake struck Haiti at 16:53 local time on Tuesday, 12 January 2010. The epicenter was near the town of Léogâne, Ouest department, approximately 25 kilometres (16 mi) west of Port-au-Prince, Haiti's capital. The earthquake is locally nicknamed Goudougoudou, an onomatopoeia for the sound of collapsing buildings.
